repo_notes.content: Do NOT generate any dedicated wiki pages or documentation for Tail Call Optimization (TCO), Trampoline, or Thunk concepts. This is currently dead code and an experimental feature. The real Tail Call Optimisation together with Continuations are in development and tracked on GitHub issue #127. Completely omit it from the documentation structure.

pages.title: Overview
pages.purpose: Introduce LIPS (Lisp Is Pretty Simple), a Scheme-based Lisp interpreter in JavaScript, explaining its purpose, design philosophy, and key features at a high level

pages.title: Installation and Quick Start
pages.purpose: Guide users through installing LIPS via npm, CDN, or standalone executable, and provide quick examples of running code in Node.js, browsers, and the REPL

pages.title: Architecture Overview
pages.purpose: Present high-level system architecture showing how the core interpreter, standard library, CLI, web components, and build system interact

pages.title: Project History and Evolution
pages.purpose: Document the evolution of LIPS through versions, major features added, breaking changes, and the roadmap for future development

pages.title: Core Interpreter
pages.purpose: Detailed documentation of the JavaScript core that implements lexing, parsing, evaluation, and the type system

pages.title: Lexer and Parser
pages.purpose: Explain the tokenization state machine, parser architecture, handling of special forms, datum labels, quasiquotation, and parser extensions

pages.title: Evaluator and Environments
pages.purpose: Document the evaluation engine, environment hierarchy, lexical vs dynamic scoping, variable binding, and special form handling

pages.title: Data Types System
pages.purpose: Detail all LIPS data types: LSymbol (with interning and gensyms), LNumber (BigInt, rationals, complex), Pair, LString, LCharacter, and special values

pages.title: Macro System
pages.purpose: Explain both Lisp macros (define-macro) and hygienic macros (syntax-rules), including pattern matching, hygiene guarantees, and macro expansion process

pages.title: CBOR Serialization
pages.purpose: Document the CBOR encoding/decoding system used for binary compilation, including structure optimization, packed values, bundled strings, and extension mechanism

pages.title: Asynchronous Operations
pages.purpose: Explain promise handling, QuotedPromise wrapper, automatic async/await, and integration with JavaScript's asynchronous programming model

pages.title: Standard Library
pages.purpose: Document the self-hosted Scheme standard library that provides core functions, macros, and R5RS/R7RS compliance

pages.title: Core Functions and Macros
pages.purpose: Detail fundamental procedures and macros like define, lambda, let, cond, map, filter, and control flow constructs

pages.title: R5RS and R7RS Compliance
pages.purpose: Explain how LIPS implements R5RS and R7RS standards through compatibility layers, including aliases and standard-specific features

pages.title: SRFI Support
pages.purpose: List built-in and loadable SRFIs, explain the @lips loading mechanism, and document each SRFI's functionality

pages.title: Object System and Records
pages.purpose: Document define-class for ES6-style classes, define-record-type for R7RS records, and the object literal syntax

pages.title: I/O and Port System
pages.purpose: Explain input/output ports, file operations, string ports, binary ports, and the buffered output system

pages.title: JavaScript Integration
pages.purpose: Document how LIPS integrates with JavaScript, enabling seamless interop between Scheme and JS code

pages.title: Accessing JavaScript Objects
pages.purpose: Explain dot notation, the new operator, the --> macro for method chaining, set! for mutations, and object literal syntax

pages.title: Promise and Async Handling
pages.purpose: Detail automatic promise resolution, promise quotation ('> syntax), and integration with JavaScript async/await

pages.title: Module Systems
pages.purpose: Document require for Node.js modules, ES module dynamic imports, and loading Scheme files with load/include

pages.title: User Interfaces
pages.purpose: Document the various ways users can interact with LIPS: command line, web browser, and bookmarklet

pages.title: Command Line Interface and REPL
pages.purpose: Explain the lips CLI executable, REPL features (history, syntax highlighting, indentation), command-line flags, and script execution

pages.title: Web-based Interactive Interpreter
pages.purpose: Document the React/TypeScript web REPL component, its integration with jQuery Terminal, examples system, and deployment

pages.title: Bookmarklet REPL
pages.purpose: Explain the bookmarklet for injecting a REPL into any webpage, its limitations, and use cases

pages.title: Development Guide
pages.purpose: Guide developers contributing to LIPS or extending it for their own projects

pages.title: Building and Distribution Pipeline
pages.purpose: Document the Makefile build system, Rollup bundling, binary compilation of standard library, and npm package structure

pages.title: Testing Framework
pages.purpose: Explain the test infrastructure using Jasmine, syntax.scm macro tests, helper utilities, and test organization

pages.title: Extensibility Mechanisms
pages.purpose: Document reader macros, parser extensions via specials map, define-symbol-macro, and custom syntax examples like defstruct
